THE ROUTES. POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request answers 204 for ANY well-formed number, known or not, and never queries the patient table at all - so membership cannot leak even through the timing of a lookup that is never performed. The only distinguishable outcomes are 400 (malformed input, which tells the caller about their own typing) and 429. Two independent limits, per client key AND per phone hash, because either alone is bypassable: one by rotating the number, the other by rotating the source. The phone limit is applied AFTER normalization, so '912345678' and '+351912345678' cannot be spent as two budgets against one handset.

POST /verify returns ONE 401 with ONE body for all five failure modes. Tested by deep-equality across them, not by both being falsy. It reaches the patient table only AFTER the code verifies - WF-07's claim time - and a test asserts linkage is never called when the code fails.

WF-07 LINKAGE. All four predicates are in the SQL rather than applied afterwards in JS, so a later edit cannot silently widen the candidate set by dropping a filter. LIMIT 2, not LIMIT 1, and that is the load-bearing detail: LIMIT 1 returns the same single row for one match and for five, silently turning an ambiguous match into a confident mis-link.

THE COST IS RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: a patient whose number sits on two rows sees exactly the same screen as someone who mistyped a digit, and cannot be told why. WF-07 accepted that. The alternative confirms to any caller that a number is in this clinic's files, and how many times.

DEGRADATION COPY. Three pt-PT strings for no phone, landline, shared number - each naming the clinic as the next step, because WF-07 is deliberately fail-closed and these will be read by real people who did nothing wrong. They are distinct from each other on purpose, which is NOT a contradiction of the identical-refusal rule: these are shown to a patient the clinic has already identified, where being specific is the remedy. The generic otp_refused stays generic and is tested against leaking any predicate.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is one thing: THE SESSION MINT. verify returns the resolved patientId and NOTHING else - no cookie, no token, asserted by test. evidence.ref: #774 MERGED 2026-08-04 (5fc88a2). The split is now even - 27s between fastest and slowest - where before the fix it ran 6m27s to 13m22s because shard 3 was spending 6.3 minutes on doomed retries, which is exactly why no figure was quoted earlier. Required check name held: 'Playwright E2E (seeded DB)' reported and passed as the aggregate, and branch protection needed NO change - the hard constraint on the whole design.

cards.notes:
Not a Wave 13 loop. Infrastructure that pays back across every PR of the wave, dispatched by the owner before LOOP 1.

THE CONSTRAINT: branch protection pins three contexts by exact string, and a check context IS a job name. Sharding the existing job in place would have renamed its checks to 'Playwright E2E (seeded DB) (1)' and friends; the required context would never report again and every PR would hang forever on a check that no longer exists. So the work moved to a job named 'E2E shard' and a new aggregate job inherits the exact old name, runs no tests, and fails unless all three shards succeeded. NO REPOSITORY SETTINGS CHANGE IS NEEDED - which was the stated fallback condition.

Workflow file and matrix only: zero test-file edits, zero playwright.config.ts edits, retries untouched (no --retries flag on pull_request, so the config's CI ? 2 : 0 still governs).

VERIFIED FROM SOURCE, NOT ASSUMED: setup runs in every shard. Pinned Playwright 1.60.0, runner/index.js:2443-2465 - the shard filter iterates rootSuite.suites, which holds top-level projects only, and dependency projects are prepended afterwards from the UNFILTERED suite. That is also why the invocation now passes --project=chromium alone: naming setup explicitly promotes it to top-level and puts its tests INTO the shard filter, the one arrangement where a shard could receive no setup tests.

THE RED PATH IS PROVEN, and not by a contrived test. A deliberate forced-failure run was planned; it turned out to be unnecessary because attempt 1 produced the exact scenario that needed proving: shard 3 genuinely failed while shards 1 and 2 passed, and the required check 'Playwright E2E (seeded DB)' went RED in 4 seconds. That is the partial-failure case - one leg red, two green - which is the one that matters and the one a designed-to-work argument could not have settled. `if: always()` plus a strict 'success' comparison behaved exactly as intended. Skipped is deliberately NOT accepted as success; this repo has already been bitten by a green that was really a skip.



--- CORRECTION AND DIAGNOSIS, 2026-08-04. THE EARLIER CHECKPOINT WAS WRONG. ---
Board checkpoint 01 (#776, merged) recorded that the cross-file-dependency hypothesis was CHECKED AND REFUTED. That was WRONG, and it was wrong because the check was too narrow: it asked who else REFERENCES the fixture constant AI_REVIEW_DRAFT, when the question that mattered was who else MUTATES the shared review queue. Correcting it here rather than leaving a merged board claim standing.

THE REAL CAUSE, proven rather than hypothesised. e2e/clinical.spec.ts:169-188 HARD-DELETES AI_DELETE_DRAFT, which fixtures.ts defines as a SECOND draft belonging to the SAME patient, Joao Pereira. e2e/revisao-consulta.spec.ts:36-39 finds its queue row by getByRole("row").filter({hasText: patientName}).first().
Unsharded, clinical.spec.ts runs BEFORE revisao-consulta.spec.ts (file order, c before r), so by the time revisao-consulta reads the queue there is exactly ONE Joao Pereira row and .first() is unambiguous.
Sharded, the local listing puts clinical.spec.ts in SHARD 1 and revisao-consulta.spec.ts in SHARD 3. AI_DELETE_DRAFT is therefore never deleted in shard 3, two Joao Pereira rows sit in the queue, and .first() selects the wrong one - whose Assumir never becomes clickable. Hence a 120s locator.click timeout, three times, 6.3 of the 10.4 minutes, which is also why shard 3 was the long pole.

THIS IS A LATENT TEST-ISOLATION DEFECT THAT SHARDING EXPOSED, NOT ONE IT CREATED. revisao-consulta.spec.ts has always depended on another spec file having run first. Any change to file order would trigger it.

PARKED per the owner ceiling of one working session. The enabling fix is one line in a TEST file - scope the row by data-record-id, exactly as clinical.spec.ts:173 already does, instead of hasText + .first() - and this PR was dispatched with zero test-file edits, so it does not belong here.

cards.title: Owner ruling R4: patient linkage is phone-match at OTP claim time, and it REFUSES on anything but exactly one match
cards.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-05 (dispatch R4, answering Q4):

"R4 - linkage mechanism (Q4): phone-match at OTP claim time, per Decision D. If EXACTLY ONE live patient row (deleted_at null, merged_into_id null, auth_user_id null) carries the proven phone, link it. Zero matches, multiple matches, or any candidate already linked: REFUSE with a clear pt-PT message directing the patient to the clinic. Card the staff-assisted activation path as post-launch. Mis-linking a medical record is the failure class the refusal exists to prevent."

WHAT IT RESOLVES. Decision D (WAVE-13.md section 1.4) makes patient login a 6-digit SMS OTP, phone only. It does not say how a proven phone number becomes a link to a patient row. Without that, LOOP 3 cannot build the claim step.

THE PREDICATE IS EXACT, and every clause of it is load-bearing. A candidate row must have deleted_at null (not soft-deleted), merged_into_id null (not the losing side of a patient merge), and auth_user_id null (not already claimed by someone). EXACTLY ONE such row must carry the proven phone. Any other count refuses. So does any candidate that is already linked - a phone reaching an already-claimed row is either a shared number or a re-registration, and neither is safe to resolve automatically.

IT IS DELIBERATELY FAIL-CLOSED AND WILL REFUSE REAL PATIENTS. Shared household numbers, a clinic row holding the wrong phone, a patient with two rows: all refuse. That is the trade the owner made explicitly, and the reason is on the ruling - mis-linking a medical record hands one patient another patient's clinical history. A refused login is an inconvenience and a phone call. A mis-link is a data breach with two named patients in it.

REQUIRED SHAPE OF THE BUILD: the refusal copy is pt-PT, in packages/i18n, and directs the patient to contact the clinic. It must NOT tell the patient which predicate failed - 'no row found' versus 'several rows found' versus 'already claimed' are three different disclosures about who else exists in the database, so the refusal is generic, exactly as the token rejection is generic under counsel's section 3. Refusal-style tests per the Decision B precedent: zero-match refuses, multi-match refuses, already-linked refuses, and the single live match links.

FOLLOW-ON CARDED: LE-staff-assisted-activation, post-launch, for the patients this legitimately locks out.

CONSUMED BY: W13-03 (LOOP 3).

cards.title: Owner ruling R5: delete sendPatientActivation - it grants a session by design and has no caller
cards.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-05 (dispatch R5, answering Q5):

"R5 - sendPatientActivation (Q5): delete it. It grants a session by design, violating Decision D, and has no caller. Include a refusal-style test where applicable, per the Decision B precedent."

WHAT IT RESOLVES. WAVE-13.md LOOP 3 step 7 makes this function's fate a decision to be taken inside the loop, and section 6 halts the loop if it turns out to have a live caller. The board has carried it as a CANDIDATE FOR OUTRIGHT DELETION since seeding. It is now decided: delete.

RE-DERIVED FROM MAIN before recording, per standing rule 1.6. A full caller search across the repo (git grep over *.ts, *.tsx, *.md) returns: the definition at apps/api/lib/auth/activation.ts:167; its own test file apps/api/lib/auth/activation.test.ts (8 references, all inside that suite); a comment at apps/api/lib/notify/registry.ts:8 that already records it as DEAD CODE with no caller; and three documentation mentions. NO PRODUCTION CALL SITE EXISTS. The halt condition in LOOP 3 section 6 is therefore not triggered.

WHY DELETION RATHER THAN LEAVING IT DORMANT. It mints a Supabase RECOVERY link and delivers it by SMS. A recovery link is a session grant. Decision D says no password, no magic link, no session minted from any other artefact. Dead code that grants a session is one route handler away from being live code that grants a session, and it is registered approved:false today only because the notification registry happens to gate it. Deleting it removes the capability rather than the permission.

SIDE EFFECT THAT CLOSES A TRACKED RESIDUAL: fallback 6 in the loud-at-boot inventory (apps/api/lib/auth/activation.ts:117, PATIENT_ACTIVATION_REDIRECT_URL silently omitted) was deliberately LEFT because the code was dead. Deleting the function retires that residual instead of fixing it. Reflect that on LE-env-sweep-scope when the deletion merges, and check whether PATIENT_ACTIVATION_CHANNEL and PATIENT_ACTIVATION_REDIRECT_URL become unreferenced.

TEST OBLIGATION. 'Refusal-style test where applicable' per the Decision B precedent: after deletion there is no function left to test, so the enforceable artefact is a test asserting that NO code path mints a Supabase recovery link or any other session for a patient. That is the property Decision D actually protects, and it survives the function it was written about.

CONSUMED BY: W13-03 (LOOP 3).

The board carries THREE: W13-04 (booking-modes) and W13-05 (terms-acceptance) as the ruling names, plus W13-02 (LOOP 2), whose gate is owner_merge precisely because persisted per-user notification state was expected to need a table, and whose DoD requires the unread count to be derived from data rather than a client-only counter. Surfaced to the owner as a batched question.

--- R8 RE-AMENDMENT, OWNER 2026-08-05 ---

The LOOP 3 storage finding is RATIFIED IN FULL: an OTP codes table, a trusted-device table, and the durable rate-limit store on the existing Postgres per WF-06. LOOP 3 is migration-bearing.

THREE APPLIES REMAIN IN TOTAL from this point: the LOOP 3 auth-storage migration, booking-modes (LOOP 4), and terms-acceptance (LOOP 5). Slugs only. Numbers are re-derived at authoring time and NEVER pre-assigned in a plan or a card - the standing rule that exists because a session-held reservation of 0053 was silently consumed by PL-31.

THE COUNT HAS NOW BEEN WRONG TWICE IN THE SAME DIRECTION, both times by omitting a loop whose storage need was recorded in the repository rather than in the plan. LOOP 2 needed a table for per-user read state; LOOP 3 needs three, and the rate limiter says so in its OWN header (apps/api/lib/rate-limit/limiter.ts:8-20: 'the OTP flow therefore needs a DURABLE shared store before it ships. That store is a pending decision'). Re-derive from the code.

The live confirm/cancel token round trip has never been observed on the deployed app

WHAT IS ALREADY PROVEN WITHOUT IT, so this is confirmatory depth and not a hole: LOOP 1's DB-gated suite proves a second redemption is refused with a byte-identical body to a forged token; that the action and the consumption record commit or roll back together, forced by colliding the token hash inside the action's transaction; that a 48h cancel token redeemed inside the cutoff is refused with the pt-PT telephone copy AND not consumed; that a 24h SMS token cannot cancel even when the request asks; and that the landing payload carries no service name for a treatment-identifying service. The route is deployed-proven and the rule is unit-proven. What is unobserved is the two together on a live token.

QUEUED in VERIFY-QUEUE as item 1 under WF-09's batching rule. Expected screen is recorded there.

WHY: the signing secret is NOT in the owner's env file - it lives only in Vercel on osteojp-platform - so exercising this would mean copying a live signing key onto a laptop for a confirmatory check that moves no gate. The parity test additionally pins the signing script's wire format to the real verifier, so the script cannot drift into signing something the server rejects.

EXERCISED NATURALLY by the first real reminder after launch, when a genuine token reaches a genuine patient. That is a better test than a synthetic one anyway.

cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-08-05 while running the template-dependency check the owner asked for. It is not a template issue; it is an auth-model one, and it is LIVE.

WHAT EXISTS. apps/portal/app/auth/login/page.tsx:63-81 defines handleMagicLink, which calls supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email, emailRedirectTo: '/auth/callback' }). cards.title: Split-shift availability: two working periods per therapist-day instead of one continuous block
cards.notes:
OWNER-APPROVED 2026-08-05. Origin: clinic admin request relayed by Ivan. No JP trip - scheduling UX, not clinical, fiscal or legal. Committed per WF-01 BEFORE any execution.

GOAL: admin sets a morning period (e.g. 08:00-13:00) and an afternoon period (e.g. 14:00-19:00) per therapist-day, so the gap between them is outside working hours and unbookable.

=== RECON VERDICT: NO SCHEMA CHANGE. NO MIGRATION. DOES NOT QUEUE BEHIND LOOP 3. ===

The data model already supports this and so does the slot engine. Re-derived from committed code, not assumed:

1. availability_templates is ALREADY a row-per-period table: (tenant, user, location, weekday, start_time, end_time) plus an optional validity window (packages/db/src/schema.ts:770-813). A split shift is simply TWO ROWS for the same weekday.

2. The unique constraint does NOT prevent that. availability_templates_dedupe_uq covers the FULL tuple INCLUDING start_time and end_time (0006_availability_timeoff.sql:14), so it blocks exact duplicate rows only. Two rows sharing (tenant, user, location, weekday) with different times are legal today. This was the load-bearing question and the answer is the reason no migration is needed.

3. The slot engine already computes over MULTIPLE windows per day. apps/web/lib/scheduling/day-availability-core.ts:82-83 does templates.filter(t => t.weekday === weekday && isWithinValidity(...)) into `working: TimeInterval[]` - the type's own comment reads 'Working windows from availability_templates (merged, sorted)'. Plural, by construction.

CONSEQUENCE FOR REQUIREMENT 5, which asked for no new semantics and no lunch concept: there is nothing to build. The between-periods gap is outside working hours automatically, because anything not inside a `working` interval already is. No code or copy anywhere needs the word lunch, and none will be added.

CONSEQUENCE FOR REQUIREMENT 2, backwards compatibility: satisfied for free and with zero risk. Every existing schedule is already one row = period 1 with no period 2. Nothing is migrated, nothing is rewritten, and a therapist keeping one continuous block is byte-identical before and after.

CONSEQUENCE FOR REQUIREMENT 6: the migration choreography does not apply, so this card does NOT wait for the LOOP 3 apply. The slug split-shift-availability is NOT reserved and no number is derived, per the standing rule that numbers are never pre-assigned - there is simply no migration to number.

SO THE REAL WORK IS THE ADMIN UI AND ITS VALIDATION, and only that:
  - Requirement 3: extend the Horarios editor in the Gerir dialog IN PLACE. Each day row gains an optional second period behind a small add affordance, removable once added. No new page, no new dialog. Space-efficient: the day list must NOT double in height for one-period therapists, so the second period is absent rather than empty-and-hidden.
  - Requirement 4: period 2 starts at or after period 1 ends, same day, no overlap. This is form-level integrity and MAY hard-block saving the SCHEDULE form. It does not touch the standing rule that availability warnings never block APPOINTMENT saves, which stays in force.
  - Write the save path so two rows are created/updated/removed cleanly, and a removed period 2 deletes its row rather than leaving a zero-length one (the start_before_end CHECK would refuse that anyway, which is a useful backstop).

PRIORITY: medium, and it NEVER preempts LOOP 3. LOOP 3 is the launch-critical path (PG1); this fills halt gaps and post-loop slots, per the owner's own sequencing.

VISUAL GATE, requirement 7: staff-visible, so WF-03 applies and the owner's screen is the DoD. On green it enters VERIFY-QUEUE as: open a therapist Gerir dialog, set a two-period day, save, re-open to confirm persistence, and confirm the agenda reflects the gap.

RECON ACCEPTED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-05 WITH VERIFICATION TEETH. The apply count stays at two (booking-modes, terms-acceptance); this card authors no migration.

CONDITION ON THE VISUAL GATE: it must exercise the FULL claim end to end, not just the new UI. The VERIFY-QUEUE entry, when built, is: Ivan sets a two-period day, SAVES, RE-OPENS to confirm persistence, and then confirms ON THE AGENDA that the between-periods gap behaves as outside working hours. That last step is the one that tests the recon rather than the screen - the claim is that the storage and the slot engine already support this, and only the agenda can show whether they do.

HALT CONDITION: if ANY layer of the claimed existing support turns out to be absent during the build - the second row not persisting, or the slot engine collapsing two windows into one - HALT LOUD. Do not improvise a schema. The no-migration verdict was derived from three specific facts (row-per-period table, dedupe constraint covering the times, day-availability-core filtering into a plural TimeInterval[]), so if it is wrong, one of those three is wrong and the right response is to say which.

DEEP RECON 2026-08-05, BEFORE BUILDING. NO HALT: all three facts the no-migration verdict rested on still hold. But a FOURTH layer exists that the verdict did not enumerate, and it is where the actual work is - recorded precisely so the next session starts from truth rather than from my earlier summary.

CONFIRMED AGAIN:
  1. availability_templates is row-per-period.
  2. The dedupe unique constraint covers the full tuple INCLUDING times, so two rows per weekday are legal.
  3. day-availability-core.ts filters into a plural working: TimeInterval[].

THE FOURTH LAYER, apps/web/app/admin/staff/page.tsx:100-118. `buildDays` builds ScheduleDay[] through a Map called firstByKey, keyed userId:weekday, which KEEPS ONLY THE FIRST TEMPLATE PER WEEKDAY. Its own comment states the intent: 'tracks exactly one id per weekday, matching the W4-14 reconcile invariant.'

THAT IS NOT A DEFECT AND NOT THE HALT CONDITION. The halt condition was 'if any layer of the claimed EXISTING SUPPORT turns out absent'. Storage and the slot engine were the claim, and both hold. buildDays is UI plumbing deliberately written to a one-row-per-day invariant - it is the thing this card exists to change, not a discovery that invalidates the verdict. The migration count stays at two.

BUT IT DOES MEAN THE WORK IS FOUR FILES, NOT TWO, and a build that only touched the modal would silently drop period 2 on every reload - the row would save and then vanish, which is the worst failure shape available here. The full set:
  a. StaffManageModal.tsx: ScheduleDay gains p2On/p2Id/p2Start/p2End (optional). Render a second
     period behind a small add affordance, removable once added. Space-efficient: ABSENT rather
     than empty-and-hidden, so a one-period therapist's row does not grow.
  b. admin/staff/page.tsx buildDays: stop collapsing. Keep the FIRST two templates per weekday,
     ordered by start_time (the loader already orders by startTime, so first = morning).
  c. horarios/actions.ts saveScheduleAction: the reconcile loop runs for BOTH periods. Same
     enabled+id -> update / enabled+no id -> create / disabled+id -> archive rules, with the
     period-2 fields posted as d{wd}p2_*. Period 2 reuses period 1's location (the card scopes
     this per therapist-day-LOCATION).
  d. Validation: p2 start >= p1 end, same day, no overlap. Form-level, MAY hard-block the
     SCHEDULE form. Does NOT touch the standing rule that availability warnings never block
     APPOINTMENT saves.

WATCH FOR: the W4-14 reconcile invariant is named in at least three comments across those files. Changing it without updating those comments leaves the next reader trusting a rule that no longer holds - the exact class of defect the stale approval packet was.

NOT STARTED. Deliberately not begun at the end of a context window: a half-built version that saves a second period the loader then discards is worse than nothing, because it looks like it works once.

GOAL: the day grid draws a faint rule at the :30 mark inside each hour row. Remove it. Hour lines only.

OBSERVED 2026-08-05 from the owner's own production query, run while finding an appointment for the token test. NOT A DEFECT, and carded as an operational observation so it is not mistaken for one.

THE DATA: status scheduled, n=14, earliest 2026-07-31 10:00, latest 2026-08-07 15:00. Alongside completed n=8, no_show n=1, cancelled n=1. So roughly a week of past appointments sits in a live state, never moved to completed or no_show.

MOST LIKELY CAUSE IS WORKFLOW, NOT CODE: reception not closing out the day. That is why this is low priority and routed to Rodica via Ivan rather than into a build queue.

TWO REAL INTERACTIONS, worth knowing before anyone 'fixes' the data:
  - listOpenSlots carries a past-slot floor that sweeps past times out of bookable slots, so these are not offered to patients. The stale status does not open a booking hole.
  - Migration 0052 made a no_show RELEASE its slot. An appointment left as scheduled never reaches that path, so the release never fires - harmless while the slot is in the past, but it means the 0052 behaviour is untested against real data.

DO NOT BULK-UPDATE THESE. Marking a past appointment completed asserts the patient attended, and marking it no_show asserts they did not; both are clinical and billing statements about a real person. Only the clinic can say which. A script that guessed would be writing false records at scale.

POST-LAUNCH, non-blocking. Nothing about launch depends on it.

cards.title: Which artefact carries the PORTAL SESSION after a verified OTP - three committed facts cannot all hold
cards.notes:
FOUND WHILE BUILDING THE SESSION MINT, 2026-08-05, and raised rather than resolved because resolving it means picking a product decision nobody has made. It does NOT block LOOP 3: none of LOOP 3 nine DoD lines requires it, and the claim transaction ships without it.

THE THREE FACTS, each re-derived from committed code, not remembered:
1. apps/api/lib/auth/patient.ts:63 getPatientPrincipal accepts ONLY a cryptographically verified SUPABASE-ISSUED JWT carrying role=patient. There is no other principal shape and no local signing key anywhere in the repo.
2. apps/api/lib/auth/no-session-minting.test.ts:41-50 scans all of apps/api and fails if ANY file mentions generateLink, signInWithPassword, signInWithOtp, setSession or admin.createUser. That test is WF-08 own artefact and it is what makes Decision D enforceable rather than aspirational.
3. apps/api/lib/auth/patient-linkage.ts:65 refuses any patient row whose auth_user_id is NOT null (WF-07). So the first successful login would set auth_user_id and EVERY LATER LOGIN BY THE SAME PATIENT WOULD REFUSE - unless the trusted device carries them, and that expires at 30 days by ruling.

A working phone-only portal login cannot satisfy all three. Something has to give, and which one is a decision with real consequences.

OPTIONS, with the trade named:
(a) The API mints the Supabase user at claim time (admin.createUser + a session), and the scan grows ONE narrow allowance on the OTP claim path. Cost: the property in fact 2 stops being absolute, and it is the only reason Decision D is enforceable today.
(b) The session becomes OURS, not Supabase - a short-lived signed cookie the API issues and getPatientPrincipal learns to accept as a second principal source. Cost: a second auth boundary to keep correct, next to the one that already had a real incident (SEC-W1-patient-jwt-verify).
(c) auth_user_id stops being the linkage key: the OTP claim links by phone and the patient never gets a Supabase auth user at all. Cost: RLS jwt_patient_id() and docs/architecture.md:360-362 both assume auth.uid() to patients.auth_user_id, so this is a change to the RLS story, not just to a column.

RECOMMENDED DEFAULT if no answer arrives: (b). It keeps fact 2 intact, keeps WF-07 refusal semantics intact, and confines the new surface to one file that can be adversarially tested the way jwt.ts already is. It is also the only option that does not touch production auth identities.

WHAT SHIPS MEANWHILE: verify returns the resolved patientId and plants the trusted-device cookie. The portal login SCREENS are not built either, and they cannot be finished without this answer, since the screen after the code is the one that needs a session.
